checks.label: The average value of a function on an interval is its definite integral divided by the interval’s length: each flat rectangle drawn has the curve’s area over the same stretch, 4 A × 2 s = 8 C under 3t², 3 A × 3 s = 9 C under t², 3 A × 2 s = 6 C under the ramp and 12 A² × 2 s = 24 under its square

The average of a whole cycle is zero: on the a.c. screen the hatched bars below the axis cancel the bars above at every bar count from 4 to 100, so their heights add up to 0 A, and the sine wave’s area over a whole cycle comes to 0

Using only half a cycle the average value is 0.637 of the peak value: for the 10 A peak the bars’ mean drawn goes 6.53, 6.41 and 6.37 A for 4, 8 and 100 bars, falling with every extra bar towards 0.637 of the peak, and the 20 A puzzle’s answer is 0.637 × 20 = 12.7 A

To find the RMS value of any function, square it, find the mean over the period, then take the square root: the ramp to 6 A gives √12 = 3.46 A, the ramp to 12 A gives √48 = 6.93 A and the 30 V sawtooth 17.3 V, each from 20,000 squared bars, and the RMS level drawn sits at that height

The RMS value of a sine wave is 0.707 of the peak value: the squared 10 A sine wave averages 50 A² over a cycle, the fold leaves its flat band at 50 A², √50 = 7.07 A and 7.07 ÷ 10 = 0.707; the RMS level drawn on the fold screen sits at 7.07 A

The RMS value of a voltage or current is the peak value divided by the square root of 2: 10 ÷ √2 = 7.07 A for the 10 A sine wave, and 100 ÷ √2 = 70.7 V in the voltage puzzle, where the RMS level drawn once it is answered sits at 70.7 V

The peak value of a sine wave is equal to 1.414 × the RMS value: an RMS of 5 A gives a peak of 5 × 1.414 = 7.07 A, the wave drawn once the puzzle is answered, and that wave’s own RMS from 20,000 squared bars is 5 A

The RMS value is the steady current that would provide the same energy: squared, the steady 7.07 A drawn on the fold screen matches the 50 A² mean of the squared sine wave, and the steady 3.46 A on the ramp screen matches the 12 A² mean of its square, so with the same resistance each heats alike

Calculates the rms value, mean value and form factor of sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal wave forms: the three-wave screen shows the square wave 10 A, 10 A and 1, the sine wave 6.37 A, 7.07 A and 1.11, and the ramp 3 A, 3.46 A and 1.15, each worked out from its wave by 20,000 bars with the means over half a cycle for the two a.c. waves; the 12 A ramp’s form factor is 6.93 ÷ 6 = 1.15

The fold fits exactly: a quarter cycle on, the squared current is always 100 minus what it is now; folded flat, every point of each hump lands on the curve of the dip it drops into with its flat side on 50 A², the humps fill every dip across the cycle, and each hump keeps its area
Every puzzle offers three different answers and accepts only the right one; each answer’s number is the value its slip gives, rounded as shown

Before Check no puzzle gives its verdict: nothing red and the working ends in a question mark; a picked answer only marks its own value; a right answer draws the answer with nothing red; every wrong answer shows its slip in red
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 5 s of its screen opening, and every pick’s or answer’s motion within 1.3 s
